properties.name: A conclusion whose every route is contested reads `contested`, not `unproven`, a word that also means refuted
properties.source: @ajs, 2026-10-18: "Capture the shortcomings (gaps) from the trial" (cogito trial)
properties.statement:
When every line of support for a claim is held up only by standing objections or contested premises, its proof status reads `contested` and names what stands against each route. `unproven` is kept for a claim with no holding route for another reason. The read-back never lets a reader take a contested conclusion for a refuted one.
Observed in the cogito trial (2026-10-18): req:i-exist read proof_status `unproven`, "no derivation holds", while all three routes were only contested. Meanwhile req:whatever-thinks-exists, in the same state, read `contested`, so the two labels disagree.
